ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part I, Ch 5 Coordination Compounds: IUPAC nomenclature of coordination compounds: order of ligands and oxidation state

subject: chemistry
stem: The total number of stereoisomers (geometrical and optical together) possible for the octahedral complex ion [Co(en)2Cl2]+, where en is ethane-1,2-diamine, a bidentate ligand, is:
explanation: The trans form has a plane of symmetry and is optically inactive. The cis form has no plane or centre of symmetry, so it exists as a pair of mirror-image optical isomers. The total is 2 + 1 = 3. Answering 2 counts only the cis and trans geometrical isomers and misses the optical pair of the cis form.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part I, Ch 5 Coordination Compounds: Stereoisomerism in coordination compounds: geometrical and optical isomers of [Co(en)2Cl2]+

subject: chemistry
stem:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I (Complex): (A) [Fe(CO)5] (B) [Cr(CO)6] (C) [Ni(CN)4]²⁻ (D) [NiCl4]²⁻
List-II (Shape): (I) Tetrahedral (II) Octahedral (III) Square planar (IV) Trigonal bipyramidal
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
explanation: Fe(CO)5 is trigonal bipyramidal (dsp³) and Cr(CO)6 is octahedral (d²sp³). Ni²⁺ forms square planar [Ni(CN)4]²⁻ with the strong-field cyanide (dsp²) but tetrahedral [NiCl4]²⁻ with the weak-field chloride (sp³). Swapping the last two shapes is the usual slip, since both are four-coordinate Ni(II) complexes.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part I, Ch 5 Coordination Compounds: Shape and bonding of metal carbonyls and of four-coordinate nickel(II) complexes

subject: chemistry
stem:
Arrange the following complex ions in the increasing order of their spin-only magnetic moment.
(A) [Fe(H2O)6]²⁺
(B) [Co(NH3)6]³⁺
(C) [Cr(H2O)6]³⁺
(D) [Ni(H2O)6]²⁺
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
explanation: Unpaired electrons give the moment √[n(n+2)]: [Co(NH3)6]³⁺ is low-spin d⁶ with 0 (0 BM), [Ni(H2O)6]²⁺ is d⁸ with 2 (2.83 BM), [Cr(H2O)6]³⁺ is d³ with 3 (3.87 BM) and [Fe(H2O)6]²⁺ is high-spin d⁶ with 4 (4.90 BM). Treating cobalt(III) as high spin would place it at the top instead of at zero.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part I, Ch 5 Coordination Compounds: Crystal field theory and Valence Bond Theory: high-spin and low-spin octahedral complexes, magnetic moment

subject: general_test
stem: C. V. Raman was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1930 for his work on:
explanation: Raman discovered that light scattered by a transparent substance contains extra wavelengths, now called the Raman effect, and received the 1930 Physics Nobel Prize for it. The photoelectric effect was explained by Einstein, who won the 1921 prize for it, so it is the neighbouring Nobel topic students confuse with Raman's work.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, General Knowledge: Awards and honours: Indian Nobel laureates in science

subject: general_test
stem: The writ of quo warranto is issued by a court to:

options.text: secure the release of a person who has been illegally detained
compel a public official to carry out a duty he has neglected
set aside the order passed by a lower court or tribunal
ask a person by what authority he holds a public office

explanation: Quo warranto literally means "by what warrant" and is used to test the legal authority of a person holding a public office. The release of an unlawfully detained person is the work of habeas corpus, a duty is enforced by mandamus, and a lower court's order is quashed by certiorari, so those three are the writs it is most often confused with.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, General Knowledge: Indian polity: fundamental rights and the writs under Articles 32 and 226

subject: general_test
stem: Which of the following rivers of peninsular India drains into the Arabian Sea?
explanation: The Tapi, like the Narmada, flows west through a rift valley and falls into the Arabian Sea, forming an estuary instead of a delta. The Mahanadi, Krishna and Kaveri all flow east and reach the Bay of Bengal, so the Kaveri is the usual trap for students who think every southern river flows west.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, General Knowledge: Indian geography: rivers and their drainage

subject: general_test
stem:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I: (A) World Environment Day (B) World Health Day (C) International Women's Day (D) Human Rights Day
List-II: (I) 8 March (II) 5 June (III) 10 December (IV) 7 April
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
explanation: World Environment Day falls on 5 June, World Health Day on 7 April, International Women's Day on 8 March and Human Rights Day on 10 December, the date the UN General Assembly adopted the Universal Declaration in 1948. The mapping that swaps 8 March with 10 December, or 5 June with 7 April, mixes up the environmental and health days with the days of rights.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, General Knowledge: Important days and years: international days and their dates

subject: general_test
stem: If the Rajya Sabha does not return a Money Bill to the Lok Sabha within 14 days of receiving it, the Bill is:

options.text: deemed passed by both Houses in the form the Lok Sabha passed it
referred to a joint sitting of both Houses to resolve the delay
treated as rejected and dropped by the Rajya Sabha
kept pending until the Rajya Sabha takes it up

explanation: Under Article 109 the Rajya Sabha can only make recommendations on a Money Bill within 14 days; if it keeps the Bill longer, the Bill is deemed passed by both Houses as the Lok Sabha passed it. A joint sitting under Article 108 is meant for ordinary Bills, so it is the tempting but wrong deadlock remedy here.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, General Knowledge: Indian polity: legislative procedure, Money Bills

subject: general_test
stem: Who founded the Arya Samaj in 1875?
explanation: Swami Dayanand Saraswati founded the Arya Samaj in Bombay in 1875 and urged a return to the Vedas. Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded the Brahmo Samaj in 1828, which is the reform society most often mixed up with it, while Vivekananda founded the Ramakrishna Mission and Vidyasagar worked for widow remarriage.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, General Knowledge: Indian history: social and religious reform movements

subject: general_test
stem:
Consider the following statements about the geography of India and its neighbourhood.
(A) Chilika Lake in Odisha is a brackish water lagoon.
(B) The Sundarbans delta is shared between India and Bangladesh.
(C) The Tropic of Cancer passes through the state of Odisha.
(D) The Western Ghats are more continuous than the Eastern Ghats.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
explanation: Chilika is a brackish lagoon joined to the Bay of Bengal, and the Sundarbans delta lies in both West Bengal and Bangladesh. The Tropic of Cancer crosses eight states from Gujarat to Mizoram but not Odisha. The Western Ghats form an almost unbroken wall, whereas the Eastern Ghats are broken by the Godavari, Krishna and other rivers.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, General Knowledge: Indian and world geography: lakes, deltas, the Tropic of Cancer and the Ghats

subject: general_test
stem: The Thomas Cup is a prestigious international team championship in which sport?
explanation: The Thomas Cup is the men's world team championship of badminton, and India won it for the first time in 2022. The women's counterpart is the Uber Cup. Table tennis has the Swaythling Cup and lawn tennis has the Davis Cup, which are the other team trophies students tend to swap with it.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, General Knowledge: Sports: trophies and championships

subject: general_test
stem: The rate at which the Reserve Bank of India lends short-term funds to commercial banks against government securities is called the:
explanation: In a repo, a bank sells government securities to the RBI and agrees to buy them back later, so the repo rate is the price of short-term borrowing from the RBI. The reverse repo rate is what the RBI pays when banks park surplus funds with it, while the cash reserve ratio and statutory liquidity ratio are reserve requirements, not lending rates.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, General Knowledge: Basic economy: RBI and monetary policy rates

subject: general_test
stem:
Arrange the following Mughal emperors in the order in which they came to the throne, earliest first.
(A) Shah Jahan
(B) Humayun
(C) Akbar
(D) Jahangir
explanation: Humayun succeeded Babur in 1530, Akbar came to the throne in 1556, Jahangir in 1605 and Shah Jahan in 1628, giving the order Humayun, Akbar, Jahangir, Shah Jahan. The ordering that puts Shah Jahan before Jahangir reverses a father and son, and the one that puts Akbar first forgets that Humayun is his father.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, General Knowledge: Indian history: the Mughal dynasty and its order of rulers

subject: general_test
stem: The Rajatarangini, a chronicle of the kings of Kashmir, was written by:
explanation: Kalhana composed the Rajatarangini in Sanskrit in the twelfth century, and it is regarded as one of the earliest works of history writing in India. Banabhatta wrote the Harshacharita, a biography of Harsha, and Vishakhadatta wrote the play Mudrarakshasa, so both are authors of other historical texts that are often confused with it.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, General Knowledge: Books and authors: classical historical texts

subject: general_test
stem: Which principal organ of the United Nations has five permanent members, each holding the power of veto?
explanation: The Security Council has five permanent members, namely China, France, Russia, the United Kingdom and the United States, and each can block a substantive resolution by veto. The General Assembly gives every member state one vote and has no veto, so it is the body students most often pick by mistake.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, General Knowledge: International organisations: principal organs of the United Nations

subject: general_test
stem: The ruins at Hampi, a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Karnataka, are the remains of the capital of the:
explanation: Hampi was the capital of the Vijayanagara Empire, founded in 1336 by Harihara and Bukka, and the city was sacked after the defeat at Talikota in 1565. The Hoysalas are linked with Halebidu and Belur, also in Karnataka, which is why that dynasty is the strongest distractor.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, General Knowledge: UNESCO sites: world heritage monuments and the dynasties behind them

subject: general_test
stem: Under the Constitution of India, the oath of office is administered to the President by the:
explanation: Article 60 requires the President to take the oath before the Chief Justice of India or, in the Chief Justice's absence, the senior-most judge of the Supreme Court available. The Vice-President is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha and has no role in the oath, which is the common slip for students who link the two top offices.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, General Knowledge: Indian polity: constitutional offices and the oath of the President

subject: general_test
stem: Madhubani painting, a traditional folk art form, originated in which Indian state?
explanation: Madhubani painting comes from the Mithila region of Bihar and is traditionally done with natural colours on walls and paper. Warli painting belongs to Maharashtra, Pattachitra to Odisha and Phad painting to Rajasthan, so each wrong state is the home of another well-known folk art.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, General Knowledge: Art and culture: folk painting traditions of India

subject: general_test
stem: India's Mars Orbiter Mission, Mangalyaan, successfully entered the orbit of Mars in which year?
explanation: The Mars Orbiter Mission was launched in November 2013 and entered Mars orbit on 24 September 2014, making India the first Asian country to reach Mars orbit. The year 2013 marks only the launch, and 2008 is the launch year of Chandrayaan-1, so these are the two dates students mix up with the arrival.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, General Knowledge: Science and technology milestones: India's space missions

subject: general_test
stem: Mount Kilimanjaro, the highest mountain in Africa, lies in:
explanation: Kilimanjaro is a dormant volcano in north-eastern Tanzania, near the border with Kenya, and rises to about 5,895 metres. Kenya is the common wrong answer because it borders Tanzania at the mountain, but Mount Kenya, the second highest peak of Africa, is a different mountain inside Kenya.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, General Knowledge: World geography: major mountains and their countries

subject: general_test
stem: Which vitamin is synthesised in the human skin on exposure to sunlight?
explanation: Ultraviolet rays in sunlight convert a cholesterol derivative in the skin into vitamin D, and a shortage of it causes rickets in children. Vitamin K is the strongest distractor because the body also makes it, but it is made by bacteria in the intestine and not by the skin.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, General Science and Environment Literacy: Basic life science: vitamins, sources and deficiency diseases

subject: general_test
stem: Which international agreement, signed in 1971, is concerned with the conservation of wetlands?
explanation: The Ramsar Convention, signed in the Iranian city of Ramsar, protects wetlands of international importance and promotes their wise use. The Montreal Protocol deals with ozone-depleting substances, the Kyoto Protocol with greenhouse gas cuts and the Basel Convention with the movement of hazardous waste, so each wrong answer is an environmental treaty with a different target.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, General Science and Environment Literacy: International environment conventions: Ramsar, Basel, Kyoto and Montreal

subject: general_test
stem:
Assertion: Depletion of the ozone layer is the main cause of global warming.
Reason: Chlorofluorocarbons are greenhouse gases as well as ozone-depleting substances.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true

explanation: The main driver of global warming is the build-up of carbon dioxide, with methane and nitrous oxide, from burning fossil fuels, and ozone depletion mainly lets more ultraviolet radiation reach the ground, so the assertion is false. The reason is true because chlorofluorocarbons both destroy ozone and trap heat, but this does not make ozone loss the main cause of warming.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, General Science and Environment Literacy: Environmental topics: greenhouse gases, global warming and the ozone layer

subject: general_test
stem: At the G20 Leaders' Summit held in New Delhi in September 2023, which of the following was admitted as a permanent member of the G20?
explanation: At the New Delhi summit in September 2023 the African Union joined the G20 as a permanent member, becoming the second regional bloc in the group after the European Union. ASEAN, the Arab League and the Commonwealth are not G20 members, so each is a regional or political grouping that students may wrongly assume sits at the table.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, Current Affairs: G20 New Delhi summit of 2023 and admission of the African Union

subject: general_test
stem: The Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, passed by Parliament in 2023, provides for reservation of one-third of the seats for women in:

options.text: Lok Sabha and State Legislative Councils
Rajya Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies
Rajya Sabha and State Legislative Councils
Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies

explanation: The Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023, known as the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, reserves one-third of the seats for women in the Lok Sabha, the State Legislative Assemblies and the Delhi Assembly. It does not cover the Rajya Sabha or the Legislative Councils, so options that include them confuse the directly elected lower houses with the upper houses.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, Current Affairs: Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, women's reservation law of 2023

subject: general_test
stem:
Consider the following statements about the three new criminal laws passed by Parliament in 2023.
(A) The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita replaces the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
(B) The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita replaces the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
(C) The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam replaces the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
(D) The three laws came into effect on 1 July 2024.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
explanation: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita replaced the Indian Penal Code, the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita replaced the Code of Criminal Procedure and the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam replaced the Indian Evidence Act; all three came into effect on 1 July 2024. Statement (C) is false because the Evidence Act, not the Penal Code, is the law the Sakshya Adhiniyam replaced, a slip the similar-sounding names invite.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, Current Affairs: the three new criminal laws of 2023 and the Acts they replace

subject: general_test
stem: In the 2024 Lok Sabha election, the BJP won 240 of the 543 seats. How many more seats would it have needed to reach a majority on its own?
explanation: A majority in a House of 543 needs more than half the seats, which is more than 271.5, so at least 272. The BJP needed 272 - 240 = 32 more seats. Working from 271 gives 31, which is one seat short of a majority, and 303 is simply the number of seats the party did not win (543 - 240).
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, Current Affairs: 2024 general election to the Lok Sabha and the majority mark

subject: general_test
stem: Puppy : Dog :: Lamb : ?
explanation: A puppy is the young one of a dog, so a lamb is the young one of a sheep. A young goat is called a kid, a young deer a fawn and a young cow a calf, so each of the other options belongs with a different young animal.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, General Mental Ability: analogy (young one and its parent)

subject: general_test
stem: Five friends P, Q, R, S and T are ranked by weight. P is heavier than Q but lighter than R. S is lighter than T, and T is lighter than Q. Who is the second lightest?
explanation: The first two facts give R > P > Q and the last two give Q > T > S, so the full order from heaviest to lightest is R, P, Q, T, S. The lightest is S and the second lightest is T. Choosing P comes from counting the second place from the heavy end instead, and Q is only the middle of the five.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, General Mental Ability: ranking and order from comparative statements

subject: general_test
stem:
Arrange the following words as they would appear in a dictionary.
(A) Planet
(B) Plant
(C) Plain
(D) Plane
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
explanation: Dictionary order compares letters from the left. All four words begin with pla, and the fourth letter puts plain (i) before the other three (n). Plane is a prefix of planet, so it comes first, and planet (e as fifth letter) comes before plant (t). The order is plain, plane, planet, plant.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, General Mental Ability: ordering words by dictionary order

subject: general_test
stem: At sunrise, Kiran stands so that his shadow falls on his left. He then turns 90° clockwise. Which direction is he facing now?
explanation: The Sun rises in the east, so a shadow at sunrise falls towards the west. With the shadow on his left, west is to his left, so Kiran faces north. A 90° clockwise turn from north points him east. Facing south would put the western shadow on his right, not his left.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, General Mental Ability: direction sense with shadows and turns

subject: general_test
stem: Pointing to Anil, Ravi says, 'He is the son of my mother's only brother.' How is Anil related to Ravi?
explanation: Ravi's mother's brother is his maternal uncle, so Anil, the maternal uncle's son, is Ravi's cousin. Calling Anil the maternal uncle mixes up the father with the son, and a nephew would be one generation younger than Ravi, whereas Anil is of the same generation.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, General Mental Ability: blood relations from a single described link

subject: general_test
stem: The ratio of boys to girls in a class is 3 : 5. If there are 12 more girls than boys, the total number of students in the class is:
explanation: Let the numbers be 3k and 5k. Their difference 2k = 12 gives k = 6, so there are 18 boys and 30 girls, and the total is 8k = 48 (check: 30 - 18 = 12). Taking 12 as the value of one part gives 96, and 18 and 30 are only the boys and only the girls.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, Basic Mathematical Concepts: ratio and proportion with a given difference

subject: general_test
stem: The diagonal of a rectangle is 13 cm and its perimeter is 34 cm. The area of the rectangle is:
explanation: Let the sides be l and b. Then l + b = 17 and l² + b² = 13² = 169, so 2lb = 17² - 169 = 289 - 169 = 120 and lb = 60 cm² (check: sides 12 and 5 give perimeter 34, diagonal 13 and area 60). The value 120 is 2lb, left without halving, and 30 is the area of the right triangle formed by half the rectangle.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, Basic Mathematical Concepts: perimeter, area and diagonal of a rectangle with the identity (l + b)² = l² + b² + 2lb

subject: general_test
stem: A sum of money amounts to ₹1,200 in 2 years at 10% per annum simple interest. The compound interest on the same sum for 2 years at 10% per annum, compounded annually, is:
explanation: Under simple interest the amount is P(1 + 2 × 0.10) = 1.2P = 1,200, so P = 1,000. With annual compounding the amount after one year is 1,100 and after two years 1,100 × 1.1 = 1,210, so the compound interest is 1,210 - 1,000 = 210. The figure 200 is the simple interest and 1,210 is the amount, not the interest.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, Basic Mathematical Concepts: simple and compound interest basics

subject: general_test
stem: Which of the following describes the Venn diagram that correctly represents Surgeons, Doctors and Women?

options.text: Doctors and Surgeons overlap partly, and Women is a separate circle
Surgeons and Women both lie wholly inside Doctors, apart from each other
Surgeons lies wholly inside Doctors, and Women cuts across both circles
Doctors lies wholly inside Surgeons, and Women cuts across both circles

explanation: Every surgeon is a doctor, so the Surgeons circle lies wholly inside the Doctors circle. Some women are doctors and some are surgeons, while other women are neither, so the Women circle must cut across both circles. Placing Women inside Doctors would claim that every woman is a doctor.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, Logical & Analytical Reasoning: Venn diagram representation of three related classes

subject: general_test
stem: At a meeting, each of 8 delegates shakes hands exactly once with every other delegate. How many handshakes take place in all?
explanation: Each handshake is one pair of delegates, so the number of handshakes is (8 x 7) / 2 = 28. The product 8 x 7 = 56 counts every handshake twice, once from each delegate. Adding 1 + 2 + ... + 8 = 36 wrongly gives the last delegate a handshake with someone new.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, Logical & Analytical Reasoning: analytical puzzle on counting handshakes among a group

subject: general_test
stem: Kabir, Lata and Meena are each either a truth-teller, who always speaks the truth, or a liar, who always lies. Kabir says, "Lata is a liar." Lata says, "Meena is a liar." Meena says, "Kabir and Lata are both liars." Who is the truth-teller?
explanation: If Meena told the truth, Kabir and Lata would both be liars, yet Kabir's claim that Lata is a liar would then be true, a contradiction. So Meena lies, which makes Lata's statement about her true; Lata is truthful, so Kabir's claim about Lata is false and Kabir lies. Only Lata is the truth-teller.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, Logical & Analytical Reasoning: truth-teller and liar puzzle with three people

subject: general_test
stem: Five friends Arun, Bela, Chetan, Divya and Esha sit on chairs numbered 1 to 5 in a line. Chetan has chair 3. Bela has the chair just before Chetan's and Divya has the chair just after it. Esha does not have chair 1. If Arun and Chetan exchange chairs, whose chair is just before Divya's?
explanation: Chetan has chair 3, Bela chair 2 and Divya chair 4. Arun and Esha must take chairs 1 and 5, and Esha cannot have chair 1, so Arun has chair 1 and Esha chair 5. After Arun and Chetan exchange chairs, Chetan has chair 1 and Arun has chair 3, which is just before Divya's chair 4. Chetan is the answer only if the exchange is ignored.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, Logical & Analytical Reasoning: linear seating arrangement and the effect of exchanging two places

subject: general_test
stem: Of 8 coins that look identical, one is slightly heavier than the others. Using only a simple balance with two pans and no weights, what is the minimum number of weighings that is certain to find the heavier coin?
explanation: Weigh 3 coins against 3. If a pan goes down, the heavy coin is among those 3; weigh two of them against each other to find it. If the pans balance, it is one of the 2 coins left aside, and one more weighing finds it. Splitting into halves each time (4 against 4, then 2 against 2, then 1 against 1) needs 3 weighings and wastes the third outcome of the balance.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, Logical & Analytical Reasoning: analytical puzzle, minimum weighings on a balance

subject: general_test
stem:
Four colleagues arrived at an office one after another on a morning. Farid arrived immediately after Esha. Dev arrived after Gauri, and Gauri was not the earliest to arrive. Arrange the colleagues in the order of arrival, beginning with the earliest.
(A) Dev
(B) Esha
(C) Farid
(D) Gauri
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
explanation: Esha and Farid arrive as a consecutive pair, and Gauri precedes Dev. If the pair came second and third, or third and fourth, Gauri would have to be the earliest, which is ruled out, so the pair arrives at the start. Gauri then arrives third and Dev fourth: Esha, Farid, Gauri, Dev. Putting Dev before Gauri breaks the second clue.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, Logical & Analytical Reasoning: ordering puzzle solved from consecutive-arrival clues

subject: general_test
stem: What is the marked price of one of the 400 notebooks?
explanation: The cost of one notebook is 20,000 / 400 = Rs 50. A mark-up of 40 per cent adds 40% of 50 = Rs 20, so the marked price is Rs 70. Rs 63 is the price after the 10 per cent discount, and Rs 90 comes from adding 40 rupees instead of 40 per cent.
passage_text: Meera runs a stationery shop. At the start of a month she borrowed Rs 20,000 at 12 per cent simple interest per annum for 6 months and spent the entire amount on 400 identical notebooks. She marked each notebook at 40 per cent above its cost price. During the month she sold 200 notebooks at a discount of 10 per cent on the marked price and the remaining 200 notebooks at the marked price. In the following month she bought the same notebooks again at the same cost, raised the marked price by 10 per cent over the earlier marked price, and then announced a festival discount of 10 per cent on the new marked price.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, Numerical Ability: profit and loss caselet, mark-up over cost price

subject: general_test
stem: According to the passage, the simple interest payable on the loan for the 6 months is:
explanation: Simple interest = P x R x T / 100 with T in years. Six months is 1/2 year, so SI = 20,000 x 12 x (1/2) / 100 = Rs 1,200. Using T = 1 gives Rs 2,400, which charges a full year, and using T = 6 gives Rs 14,400 by reading months as years.
passage_text: Meera runs a stationery shop. At the start of a month she borrowed Rs 20,000 at 12 per cent simple interest per annum for 6 months and spent the entire amount on 400 identical notebooks. She marked each notebook at 40 per cent above its cost price. During the month she sold 200 notebooks at a discount of 10 per cent on the marked price and the remaining 200 notebooks at the marked price. In the following month she bought the same notebooks again at the same cost, raised the marked price by 10 per cent over the earlier marked price, and then announced a festival discount of 10 per cent on the new marked price.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, Numerical Ability: simple interest for a period given in months

subject: general_test
stem: According to the passage, the total amount Meera received from selling the 400 notebooks in the first month was:
explanation: The discounted price is 90% of the marked price: 0.90 x 70 = Rs 63. Revenue = 200 x 63 + 200 x 70 = 12,600 + 14,000 = Rs 26,600. Rs 28,000 ignores the discount and Rs 25,200 gives the discount on all 400 notebooks.
passage_text: Meera runs a stationery shop. At the start of a month she borrowed Rs 20,000 at 12 per cent simple interest per annum for 6 months and spent the entire amount on 400 identical notebooks. She marked each notebook at 40 per cent above its cost price. During the month she sold 200 notebooks at a discount of 10 per cent on the marked price and the remaining 200 notebooks at the marked price. In the following month she bought the same notebooks again at the same cost, raised the marked price by 10 per cent over the earlier marked price, and then announced a festival discount of 10 per cent on the new marked price.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, Numerical Ability: discount on the marked price for part of the stock

subject: general_test
stem: According to the passage, her profit per cent on the cost of the 400 notebooks in the first month was:
explanation: Profit = 26,600 - 20,000 = Rs 6,600, so profit per cent = 6,600 / 20,000 x 100 = 33%. Subtracting the discount from the mark-up (40 - 10 = 30) is wrong because the discount applies only to half the notebooks and to the marked price, not to the cost.
passage_text: Meera runs a stationery shop. At the start of a month she borrowed Rs 20,000 at 12 per cent simple interest per annum for 6 months and spent the entire amount on 400 identical notebooks. She marked each notebook at 40 per cent above its cost price. During the month she sold 200 notebooks at a discount of 10 per cent on the marked price and the remaining 200 notebooks at the marked price. In the following month she bought the same notebooks again at the same cost, raised the marked price by 10 per cent over the earlier marked price, and then announced a festival discount of 10 per cent on the new marked price.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, Numerical Ability: overall profit per cent on cost price

subject: general_test
stem: According to the passage, in the following month her profit on each notebook sold at the festival price is:
explanation: The new marked price is 70 x 1.10 = Rs 77, and the festival price is 77 x 0.90 = Rs 69.30, so the profit is 69.30 - 50 = Rs 19.30. The 10 per cent rise and the 10 per cent discount act on different bases, so they do not cancel, which would wrongly give Rs 20.00.
passage_text: Meera runs a stationery shop. At the start of a month she borrowed Rs 20,000 at 12 per cent simple interest per annum for 6 months and spent the entire amount on 400 identical notebooks. She marked each notebook at 40 per cent above its cost price. During the month she sold 200 notebooks at a discount of 10 per cent on the marked price and the remaining 200 notebooks at the marked price. In the following month she bought the same notebooks again at the same cost, raised the marked price by 10 per cent over the earlier marked price, and then announced a festival discount of 10 per cent on the new marked price.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, Numerical Ability: successive percentage changes in price and the resulting profit

subject: general_test
stem: What is the smallest number greater than 100 that leaves a remainder of 3 when divided by 6, by 8 and by 10?
explanation: Numbers leaving remainder 3 with all three divisors are of the form (LCM of 6, 8 and 10) x k + 3. The LCM is 120, so the numbers are 3, 123, 243 and so on, and the smallest above 100 is 123. The LCM itself, 120, leaves remainder 0, and 117 leaves remainder 5 with 8.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, Quantitative Reasoning: number system, LCM and a common remainder

subject: general_test
stem: Six workers can finish a job in 20 days. After 5 days, 3 more workers join them, all working at the same rate. In how many days from the start is the job finished?
explanation: The job is 6 x 20 = 120 worker-days. In 5 days the 6 workers do 30 worker-days, leaving 90, which 9 workers finish in 10 days, so the total is 5 + 10 = 15 days. The figure 10 days forgets the first 5 days, and 13 1/3 days wrongly lets all 9 workers start together.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, Quantitative Reasoning: time and work with workers joining later

subject: general_test
stem: A shopkeeper sells two articles at Rs 1,200 each, gaining 20 per cent on one and losing 20 per cent on the other. His overall result is:
explanation: The cost of the first article is 1,200 / 1.20 = Rs 1,000 and of the second is 1,200 / 0.80 = Rs 1,500. Total cost is Rs 2,500 against sales of Rs 2,400, a loss of Rs 100. Equal percentages do not cancel because they apply to different cost prices, and the 4% loss is on cost, not on sales (4% of 2,400 is 96).
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, Quantitative Reasoning: profit and loss on two articles sold at the same price

subject: general_test
stem: In an election between two candidates, the winner got 55 per cent of the valid votes and won by 1,200 votes. How many valid votes were cast?
explanation: The loser got 45%, so the winning margin is 55 - 45 = 10% of the valid votes. Then 10% of the votes = 1,200, so the valid votes are 12,000. The figure 6,600 is the winner's own tally (55% of 12,000), and 24,000 treats the margin as 5%.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, Quantitative Reasoning: percentage, winning margin in an election

subject: general_test
stem: A room is 8 m long, 6 m wide and 3 m high. What is the cost of whitewashing its four walls at Rs 15 per m²?
explanation: The four walls have area 2 x (8 + 6) x 3 = 84 m², so the cost is 84 x 15 = Rs 1,260. Adding the ceiling (48 m²) gives 132 m² and Rs 1,980, and multiplying the volume 144 by 15 gives Rs 2,160, which mixes up area and volume.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, Quantitative Reasoning: mensuration, area of the four walls of a room

subject: general_test
stem: The monthly budget of a school club is Rs 1,20,000. In a pie chart of its spending, the sector for decoration has a central angle of 54°. The amount spent on decoration is:
explanation: A full circle is 360°, so the decoration sector is 54 / 360 = 15% of the budget. Then 15% of Rs 1,20,000 = Rs 18,000. Reading 54° as 54% gives Rs 64,800, and dividing by 180° instead of 360° gives Rs 36,000.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, Statistical Data Analysis: pie chart, central angle and share of the total

subject: general_test
stem: A bar chart shows the number of visitors to a science fair: 5,000 on Friday, 9,000 on Saturday and 7,200 on Sunday. Sunday's visitors were fewer than Saturday's by:
explanation: The fall from Saturday to Sunday is 9,000 - 7,200 = 1,800 visitors. Percentage change is measured on the earlier figure, so 1,800 / 9,000 x 100 = 20%. Using Sunday as the base gives 25%, and using Friday as the base gives 36%.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, Statistical Data Analysis: percentage change read from a described bar chart

subject: general_test
stem: The mean of five numbers is 18. The largest number is 30 and the range is 22. What is the sum of the three numbers other than the largest and the smallest?
explanation: The sum of all five numbers is 5 x 18 = 90. The range is largest minus smallest, so the smallest is 30 - 22 = 8. The middle three add up to 90 - 30 - 8 = 52. Removing only the largest leaves 60, and subtracting the range itself gives 68.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, Statistical Data Analysis: mean and range of a small data set

subject: mathematics
stem: The remainder when 345 × 29 is divided by 8 is:
explanation: 345 = 43 × 8 + 1, so 345 ≡ 1 (mod 8), and 29 = 3 × 8 + 5, so 29 ≡ 5 (mod 8). The remainder of a product is the product of the remainders: 1 × 5 = 5 (check: 345 × 29 = 10005 = 1250 × 8 + 5). Adding the remainders gives 6, which is the remainder of the sum 345 + 29 = 374, not of the product.
ncert_ref: CUET 2026 Applied Mathematics syllabus, Unit I Numbers, Quantification and Numerical Applications: modulo arithmetic, remainder of a product

subject: mathematics
stem: How many integers x with 1 ≤ x ≤ 60 satisfy x ≡ 3 (mod 7)?
explanation: x ≡ 3 (mod 7) means x = 7m + 3 for an integer m. The values from 1 to 60 are 3, 10, 17, 24, 31, 38, 45, 52 and 59, that is m = 0 to 8, so there are 9. Taking the integer part of 60 ÷ 7 gives 8, which forgets that m = 0 also counts, and m = 9 would give 66, beyond 60.
ncert_ref: CUET 2026 Applied Mathematics syllabus, Unit I Numbers, Quantification and Numerical Applications: congruence modulo, integers in a residue class

subject: mathematics
stem: In what ratio must tea costing ₹ 60 per kg be mixed with tea costing ₹ 80 per kg so that the mixture is worth ₹ 72 per kg?
explanation: By the rule of allegation, cheaper : dearer = (dearer price − mean price) : (mean price − cheaper price) = (80 − 72) : (72 − 60) = 8 : 12 = 2 : 3. Check: 2 kg at ₹ 60 and 3 kg at ₹ 80 cost 120 + 240 = ₹ 360, and 360 ÷ 5 = ₹ 72 per kg. The ratio 3 : 2 writes the two differences the wrong way round, and 1 : 1 would give a mean price of ₹ 70.
ncert_ref: CUET 2026 Applied Mathematics syllabus, Unit I Numbers, Quantification and Numerical Applications: allegation and mixture, ratio of mixing

subject: mathematics
stem: A boat takes 6 hours to cover 24 km upstream and 4 hours to cover the same distance downstream. The speed of the stream is:
explanation: Upstream speed = 24 ÷ 6 = 4 km/h and downstream speed = 24 ÷ 4 = 6 km/h. Speed of the stream = (downstream − upstream) ÷ 2 = (6 − 4) ÷ 2 = 1 km/h, while the speed of the boat in still water is (6 + 4) ÷ 2 = 5 km/h. Answering 2 km/h forgets to halve the difference, and 5 km/h is the boat’s own speed.
ncert_ref: CUET 2026 Applied Mathematics syllabus, Unit I Numbers, Quantification and Numerical Applications: boats and streams, speed of the current

subject: mathematics
stem: Pipe A can fill an empty tank in 12 hours and pipe B can fill it in 20 hours, while an outlet pipe C can empty the full tank in 30 hours. If all three pipes are opened together, the empty tank will be filled in:
explanation: In one hour A fills 1/12, B fills 1/20 and C empties 1/30 of the tank. Net rate = 1/12 + 1/20 − 1/30 = (5 + 3 − 2)/60 = 1/10 of the tank per hour, so the tank fills in 10 hours. Ignoring the outlet gives 60/8 = 7.5 hours, and treating the outlet as another inlet gives 6 hours.
ncert_ref: CUET 2026 Applied Mathematics syllabus, Unit I Numbers, Quantification and Numerical Applications: pipes and cisterns, filling and emptying together

subject: mathematics
stem: In a 500 m race A beats B by 50 m, and in another 500 m race B beats C by 50 m. If each runner keeps a constant speed, by how many metres does A beat C in a 500 m race?
explanation: When A runs 500 m, B runs 450 m; when B runs 500 m, C runs 450 m. So when B runs 450 m, C runs 450 × 450/500 = 405 m. Hence C covers only 405 m while A covers 500 m, and A wins by 500 − 405 = 95 m (the speed ratios 10 : 9 and 10 : 9 give A : C = 100 : 81, the same result). Adding the two margins to get 100 m ignores that B’s second 50 m lead is measured over 500 m, not over the 450 m it runs here.
ncert_ref: CUET 2026 Applied Mathematics syllabus, Unit I Numbers, Quantification and Numerical Applications: races and games, beating by a distance

subject: mathematics
stem:
Consider the following statements about numerical inequalities, where a, b and c are real numbers.
(A) If a > b, then a + c > b + c for every value of c.
(B) If a > b, then ac > bc for every value of c.
(C) If a > b and c < 0, then ac < bc.
(D) If a > b > 0, then 1/a < 1/b.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
explanation: Adding the same number to both sides never changes an inequality, so (A) is true, and multiplying both sides by a negative number reverses it, so (C) is true. For positive numbers the larger one has the smaller reciprocal (2 > 1 but 1/2 < 1), so (D) is true. Statement (B) fails for c = 0 and for every negative c, which is the common slip of forgetting that the sign reverses for a negative multiplier.
ncert_ref: CUET 2026 Applied Mathematics syllabus, Unit I Numbers, Quantification and Numerical Applications: numerical inequalities, properties of inequalities

subject: mathematics
stem: A is 50% more efficient than B. Working together, A and B can complete a piece of work in 12 days. How many days would B alone take to complete the work?
explanation: The efficiencies of A and B are in the ratio 150 : 100 = 3 : 2, so together they do 3 + 2 = 5 units of work a day. Total work = 5 × 12 = 60 units, and B alone does 2 units a day, so B takes 60 ÷ 2 = 30 days. Check: 1/20 + 1/30 = 5/60 = 1/12. The 20 days is the time A alone would take, not B.
ncert_ref: CUET 2026 Applied Mathematics syllabus, Unit I Numbers, Quantification and Numerical Applications: numerical problems, time and work with relative efficiency

subject: mathematics
stem: A perpetuity pays ₹ 6,000 at the end of every year for ever. If the rate of interest is 8% per annum, its present value is:
explanation: The present value of a perpetuity is the payment divided by the rate of interest: 6,000 ÷ 0.08 = ₹ 75,000. Check: ₹ 75,000 invested at 8% earns exactly ₹ 6,000 a year with the capital left intact. Multiplying 6,000 by 0.08 gives ₹ 480, which is a year’s interest on the payment and not the sum needed to fund it.
ncert_ref: CUET 2026 Applied Mathematics syllabus, Unit VII Financial Mathematics: perpetuity, present value of a perpetuity

subject: mathematics
stem: A loan of ₹ 60,000 is taken at 10% per annum flat rate for 2 years and is repaid in equal monthly instalments. The EMI under the flat rate method is:
explanation: Under the flat rate method interest is charged on the original principal for the whole period: 60,000 × 10% × 2 = ₹ 12,000. Total repayment = 60,000 + 12,000 = ₹ 72,000, and spreading it over 2 × 12 = 24 months gives 72,000 ÷ 24 = ₹ 3,000. The figure ₹ 2,500 is the principal alone divided by 24, leaving out the interest.
ncert_ref: CUET 2026 Applied Mathematics syllabus, Unit VII Financial Mathematics: EMI by the flat rate method

subject: mathematics
stem: A firm deposits an equal amount at the end of each year for 2 years in a sinking fund that earns 10% per annum compound interest, so as to have ₹ 46,200 at the end of the 2nd year. The yearly deposit is:
explanation: The first deposit earns one year’s interest, so the fund after 2 years is P × 1.1 + P = 2.1P. Setting 2.1P = 46,200 gives P = ₹ 22,000; check: 22,000 × 1.1 + 22,000 = 24,200 + 22,000 = 46,200. Dividing 46,200 by 2 gives ₹ 23,100, which ignores the interest the fund earns.
ncert_ref: CUET 2026 Applied Mathematics syllabus, Unit VII Financial Mathematics: sinking fund, periodic deposit

subject: mathematics
stem:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I:
(A) Perpetuity
(B) Sinking fund
(C) Rate of return
(D) Straight-line depreciation
List-II:
(I) Gain on an investment, income plus rise in value, as a percentage of the amount invested
(II) Equal amount written off an asset’s cost in every year of its useful life
(III) Money built up by regular deposits to meet a liability on a future date
(IV) Equal payments continuing for ever at regular intervals
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
explanation: A perpetuity is a stream of equal payments with no end, a sinking fund is built from regular deposits so that a liability can be met on a fixed date, the rate of return compares income plus change in value with the sum invested, and straight-line depreciation writes off (cost − residual value) ÷ life equally each year. Linking the sinking fund with the equal yearly write-off confuses a fund that is built up with an expense that is charged.
ncert_ref: CUET 2026 Applied Mathematics syllabus, Unit VII Financial Mathematics: perpetuity, sinking fund, rate of return and linear depreciation terms

subject: mathematics
stem: The value of a fund grows by 25% in the first year and by 80% in the second year. Its compound annual growth rate (CAGR) over the two years is:
explanation: Over two years the value is multiplied by 1.25 × 1.80 = 2.25. CAGR is the constant yearly rate that gives this growth: (1 + g)² = 2.25, so 1 + g = 1.5 and g = 50%. Check: 1.5 × 1.5 = 2.25. The average of 25% and 80% is 52.5%, and the total gain of 125% divided by 2 is 62.5%; neither is a compound rate.
ncert_ref: CUET 2026 Applied Mathematics syllabus, Unit VII Financial Mathematics: compound annual growth rate versus simple annual growth rate

subject: mathematics
stem: A machine bought for ₹ 1,80,000 has a residual value of ₹ 30,000 and a useful life of 5 years. Using the straight-line method, its book value at the end of 2 years is:
explanation: Annual depreciation = (cost − residual value) ÷ useful life = (1,80,000 − 30,000) ÷ 5 = ₹ 30,000. After 2 years the total depreciation is ₹ 60,000, so the book value is 1,80,000 − 60,000 = ₹ 1,20,000. The figure ₹ 60,000 is only the depreciation charged so far, and ignoring the residual value gives ₹ 36,000 a year and a book value of 1,80,000 − 72,000 = ₹ 1,08,000.
ncert_ref: CUET 2026 Applied Mathematics syllabus, Unit VII Financial Mathematics: linear (straight line) depreciation, cost, residual value and useful life

subject: mathematics
stem: A discrete random variable X takes the values 1, 2 and 3 with probabilities 0.2, 0.5 and 0.3 respectively. The variance of X is:
explanation: The mean is E(X) = 1(0.2) + 2(0.5) + 3(0.3) = 2.1 and E(X²) = 1(0.2) + 4(0.5) + 9(0.3) = 4.9. The variance is E(X²) − [E(X)]² = 4.9 − 4.41 = 0.49. The value 4.90 is E(X²) before the squared mean is subtracted, and 0.70 is the standard deviation, not the variance.
ncert_ref: CUET 2026 Applied Mathematics syllabus, Unit IV Probability Distributions: variance and standard deviation of a discrete random variable

subject: mathematics
stem: The mean and variance of a binomial distribution are 6 and 4.5 respectively. The number of trials n is:
explanation: For a binomial distribution the mean is np and the variance is npq, so q = variance ÷ mean = 4.5/6 = 3/4 and p = 1 − q = 1/4. Then n = mean ÷ p = 6 ÷ (1/4) = 24; check: npq = 24 × 1/4 × 3/4 = 4.5. Taking 3/4 as p, which swaps p and q, gives n = 6 ÷ (3/4) = 8.
ncert_ref: CUET 2026 Applied Mathematics syllabus, Unit IV Probability Distributions: binomial distribution, mean np and variance npq

subject: mathematics
stem:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I:
(A) Mean of a binomial distribution with n = 10 and p = 0.4
(B) Variance of a binomial distribution with n = 12 and p = 0.5
(C) Variance of a Poisson distribution with mean 6
(D) Variance of the standard normal distribution
List-II:
(I) 3
(II) 6
(III) 1
(IV) 4
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
explanation: The binomial mean is np = 10 × 0.4 = 4 and the binomial variance is npq = 12 × 0.5 × 0.5 = 3. A Poisson distribution has variance equal to its mean, so 6, and the standard normal variate has mean 0 and variance 1. Using np = 6 for the binomial with n = 12 gives its mean rather than its variance.
ncert_ref: CUET 2026 Applied Mathematics syllabus, Unit IV Probability Distributions: mean and variance of binomial, Poisson and standard normal distributions

subject: mathematics
stem: A Poisson variate X satisfies E(X²) = 12. The variance of X is:
explanation: For a Poisson distribution the mean and the variance both equal λ, so E(X²) = variance + (mean)² = λ + λ². Then λ² + λ − 12 = 0, that is (λ + 4)(λ − 3) = 0, and since λ > 0, λ = 3 and the variance is 3. The value 12 is E(X²) itself, and 9 is λ² rather than the variance.
ncert_ref: CUET 2026 Applied Mathematics syllabus, Unit IV Probability Distributions: Poisson distribution, mean and variance both equal to λ

subject: mathematics
stem: The heights of plants in a nursery are normally distributed with mean 40 cm and standard deviation 5 cm. Approximately what percentage of the plants have heights between 35 cm and 45 cm?
explanation: The limits 35 cm and 45 cm give z = (35 − 40)/5 = −1 and z = (45 − 40)/5 = +1, so they lie within one standard deviation of the mean. About 68% of a normal distribution lies within μ ± σ. The figure 95% belongs to μ ± 2σ, which would be 30 cm to 50 cm.
ncert_ref: CUET 2026 Applied Mathematics syllabus, Unit IV Probability Distributions: normal distribution, standard normal variate and the 68-95-99.7 area relationship

subject: mathematics
stem: Sales of woollen garments rise every winter and fall every summer, year after year. This regular pattern repeating within each year is called:
explanation: Seasonal variation is the regular rise and fall that repeats within a year because of weather, festivals or customs, so woollen sales peaking every winter fit it. Cyclical variation spreads over several years like a business cycle, a secular trend is the long-term movement, and irregular variation is random, such as a flood or a strike. Repetition inside each year rules out cyclical variation.
ncert_ref: CUET 2026 Applied Mathematics syllabus, Unit V Time Based Data: components of a time series, seasonal variation

subject: mathematics
stem: The first two values of a time series are 10 and 15. Its 3-year moving averages for the second and third years are 17 and 19. The fourth value of the series is:
explanation: A 3-year moving average is the mean of three consecutive values. From the second average, 3 × 17 = 51 = 10 + 15 + third value, so the third value is 26. From the third average, 3 × 19 = 57 = 15 + 26 + fourth value, so the fourth value is 16. Adding 3 × (19 − 17) = 6 to the second value gives 21, which is wrong because the first value is the one that drops out of the window.
ncert_ref: CUET 2026 Applied Mathematics syllabus, Unit V Time Based Data: moving average method of measuring trend

subject: mathematics
stem: The annual output (in thousand units) of a firm over five consecutive years is 10, 14, 19, 20 and 22. A straight-line trend y = a + bt is fitted by the method of least squares with the middle year as origin and t = −2, −1, 0, 1, 2. The trend value for the last year (in thousand units) is:
explanation: Here a = Σy/5 = 85/5 = 17 and b = Σty/Σt² = (−20 − 14 + 0 + 20 + 44)/10 = 3, so the trend line is y = 17 + 3t. For the last year t = 2, the trend value is 17 + 6 = 23. The value 22 is the observed output, not the trend value, and dividing Σty by 5 instead of Σt² gives b = 6 and the wrong value 29.
ncert_ref: CUET 2026 Applied Mathematics syllabus, Unit V Time Based Data: least squares linear trend and interpreting trend values

subject: mathematics
stem: A list of 400 students is numbered 1 to 400. A systematic sample of 20 students is drawn by starting at the student numbered 6 and then selecting every kth student. The number of the fourth student selected is:
explanation: In systematic sampling the interval is k = N/n = 400/20 = 20. Starting at 6, the selected students are numbered 6, 26, 46 and 66, so the fourth is 66. The number 46 is only the third student selected, and 80 comes from ignoring the starting point (4 × 20).
ncert_ref: CUET 2026 Applied Mathematics syllabus, Unit VI Inferential Statistics: systematic sampling, selecting every kth unit

subject: mathematics
stem: A population has 6 units. The number of different simple random samples of size 3 that can be drawn without replacement, the order of selection being ignored, is:
explanation: A sample drawn without replacement is a subset of the population, so the number of samples is 6C3 = (6 × 5 × 4) ÷ (3 × 2 × 1) = 20. The value 120 = 6 × 5 × 4 counts ordered selections, 216 = 6³ is the count when each unit is put back after a draw, and 18 is 6 × 3.
ncert_ref: CUET 2026 Applied Mathematics syllabus, Unit VI Inferential Statistics: simple random sampling, number of possible samples

subject: mathematics
stem: A sample of 16 values has mean 53 and standard deviation 4.8. To test H0: μ = 50 against H1: μ ≠ 50 at the 5% level, the table value of t for 15 degrees of freedom is 2.13. The calculated t and the decision are:
explanation: The standard error is s/√n = 4.8/4 = 1.2, so t = (53 − 50)/1.2 = 2.5. This exceeds the table value 2.13, so H0 is rejected. Dividing by s instead of s/√n gives 0.625, and dividing by s/n = 0.3 gives 10; neither is the t statistic.
ncert_ref: CUET 2026 Applied Mathematics syllabus, Unit VI Inferential Statistics: one-sample t statistic and testing a null hypothesis

subject: mathematics
stem: The matrix [0 9 a; −9 0 7; 8 b 0] is skew-symmetric. The value of a + b is:
explanation: In a skew-symmetric matrix aij = −aji and the diagonal entries are zero. Here a13 = a and a31 = 8 give a = −8, while a23 = 7 and a32 = b give b = −7, so a + b = −15. Keeping the signs equal, as in a symmetric matrix, would give a = 8 and b = 7 and the wrong sum 15.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Mathematics Part I, Ch 3 Matrices: skew-symmetric matrices, Aᵀ = −A

subject: mathematics
stem: Match List-I with List-II. List-I: (A) Scalar matrix (B) Skew-symmetric matrix (C) Row matrix (D) Column matrix. List-II: (I) Aᵀ = −A (II) Order 1 × n (III) Order m × 1 (IV) Diagonal matrix with all diagonal entries equal. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
explanation: A scalar matrix is a diagonal matrix whose diagonal entries are all equal, a skew-symmetric matrix satisfies Aᵀ = −A, a row matrix has a single row so its order is 1 × n, and a column matrix has a single column so its order is m × 1. Swapping the row and column matrices is the usual slip, because both have only one line of entries.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Mathematics Part I, Ch 3 Matrices: types of matrices and their defining properties

subject: mathematics
stem: The matrices A = [2 1; 6 3] and B = [1 k; −2 4] satisfy AB = O, the zero matrix. The value of k is:
explanation: AB has first row (2 × 1 + 1 × (−2), 2 × k + 1 × 4) = (0, 2k + 4) and second row (6 × 1 + 3 × (−2), 6 × k + 3 × 4) = (0, 6k + 12). Both vanish only when k = −2. The product of two non-zero matrices can be the zero matrix because A is singular, and k = −4 comes from dropping the factor 2 in 2k + 4 = 0.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Mathematics Part I, Ch 3 Matrices: product of non-zero matrices can be the zero matrix

subject: mathematics
stem: The inverse of the matrix [6 5; 2 2] is:
explanation: For the given matrix A, |A| = 6 × 2 − 5 × 2 = 2. The inverse is (1/|A|) × adj A, and adj A swaps the diagonal entries and changes the signs of the off-diagonal ones, so A⁻¹ = (1/2) × [2 −5; −2 6]. Leaving out the factor 1/|A| gives the adjoint itself, which is not the inverse.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Mathematics Part I, Ch 3 Matrices: inverse of a 2 × 2 matrix using the adjoint

subject: mathematics
stem: For A = [1 2; 0 1] and B = [1 0; 2 1], the matrix (A + B)² − (A² + 2AB + B²) equals:
explanation: Since (A + B)² = A² + AB + BA + B², the required difference is BA − AB. Here AB = [5 2; 2 1] and BA = [1 2; 2 5], so BA − AB = [−4 0; 0 4]. The zero matrix would hold only if AB = BA, but matrix multiplication is not commutative in general.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Mathematics Part I, Ch 3 Matrices: non-commutativity of matrix multiplication

subject: mathematics
stem:
Consider the following statements about determinants of square matrices.
(A) Interchanging any two rows of a determinant changes its sign.
(B) |A + B| = |A| + |B| for any two square matrices A and B of the same order.
(C) If A is non-singular, then |A⁻¹| = 1/|A|.
(D) A square matrix with two identical columns is singular.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
explanation: Swapping two rows flips the sign of a determinant, |A||A⁻¹| = |I| = 1 gives |A⁻¹| = 1/|A|, and two equal columns make the determinant 0, so that matrix is singular. The sum rule is false: determinants multiply, |AB| = |A||B|, but |A + B| is not |A| + |B|; for order 2, |I + I| = 4 while |I| + |I| = 2.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Mathematics Part I, Ch 4 Determinants: properties of determinants, singular matrices and |A⁻¹|

subject: mathematics
stem: For what value of k does the system of equations 2x + 3y = 5 and 4x + ky = 9 have no solution?
explanation: The coefficient determinant is 2k − 12, which is zero only for k = 6. For k = 6 the second equation reads 4x + 6y = 9, while twice the first gives 4x + 6y = 10, so the two equations contradict and there is no solution. Any other k gives a non-zero determinant and a unique solution; k = 3/2 comes from inverting the ratio of coefficients.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Mathematics Part I, Ch 4 Determinants: consistency and number of solutions of a system of linear equations

subject: mathematics
stem: A and B are square matrices of order 3 with |A| = 3 and |B| = 2, and B is invertible. The value of |2AB⁻¹| is:
explanation: For order n = 3, |kM| = k^n |M|, so |2AB⁻¹| = 2³ × |A| × |B⁻¹| = 8 × 3 × (1/2) = 12, because |B⁻¹| = 1/|B|. Taking the factor as 2 instead of 2³ gives 3, treating |B⁻¹| as |B| gives 48, and leaving out B⁻¹ altogether gives 24.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Mathematics Part I, Ch 4 Determinants: |kA| = k^n |A|, |AB| = |A||B| and the determinant of an inverse

subject: mathematics
stem: Match List-I with List-II. List-I: (A) Decision variables (B) Feasible solution (C) Unbounded feasible region (D) Infeasible problem. List-II: (I) A point satisfying all the constraints and the non-negativity conditions (II) Quantities whose values are to be found to optimise the objective function (III) No point satisfies all the constraints together (IV) Region extends indefinitely in some direction. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
explanation: Decision variables are the quantities to be found to optimise the objective function, a feasible solution satisfies every constraint including non-negativity, an unbounded feasible region extends indefinitely in some direction, and an infeasible problem has no point satisfying all the constraints. Confusing a feasible solution with an infeasible problem is the common slip: the first is one valid point, the second means there is none.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Mathematics Part II, Ch 12 Linear Programming: terminology: decision variables, feasible and infeasible solutions, unbounded region

subject: mathematics
stem: Which of the following points lies in the feasible region of the constraints 2x + y ≤ 10, x + 3y ≤ 15, x ≥ 0 and y ≥ 0?
explanation: A point is feasible only if it satisfies every constraint. The point (2, 3) gives 2 × 2 + 3 = 7 ≤ 10 and 2 + 3 × 3 = 11 ≤ 15. Both (4, 3) and (5, 1) break the first constraint (11 > 10), and (2, 5) breaks the second (17 > 15), so each of them passes only one of the two checks.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Mathematics Part II, Ch 12 Linear Programming: feasible solutions and the feasible region

subject: mathematics
stem: A bakery makes x batches of bread and y batches of cake in a day. A batch of bread uses 3 kg of flour and a batch of cake uses 2 kg. Only 30 kg of flour is available, and at least 4 batches of bread must be made. Besides x ≥ 0 and y ≥ 0, the constraints are:
explanation: The flour used, 3x + 2y, cannot exceed the 30 kg available, so 3x + 2y ≤ 30. The phrase "at least 4 batches of bread" is a lower limit, so x ≥ 4. Writing 3x + 2y ≥ 30 reverses the resource limit, and x ≤ 4 reverses the minimum requirement; 2x + 3y swaps the flour used per batch.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Mathematics Part II, Ch 12 Linear Programming: mathematical formulation of a linear programming problem from words

subject: mathematics
stem: To minimise its cost Z = 5x + 2y (in rupees), a firm must satisfy 2x + y ≥ 8, x + 2y ≥ 10, x ≥ 0 and y ≥ 0. The least possible cost is:
explanation: The feasible region is unbounded, but Z has positive coefficients, so a minimum exists and lies at a corner point. The corners are (0, 8), (2, 4) and (10, 0), where Z = 16, 18 and 50, so the minimum is 16. The value 18 comes from using only the intersection of the two lines and ignoring the corner on the y-axis.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Mathematics Part II, Ch 12 Linear Programming: corner point method on an unbounded feasible region

subject: mathematics
stem: How many corner points does the region defined by 0 ≤ x ≤ 4, 0 ≤ y ≤ 4, x + y ≤ 6 and x + 2y ≤ 20 have?
explanation: The lines x + y = 6, x = 4 and y = 4 with the two axes enclose a region with corner points (0, 0), (4, 0), (4, 2), (2, 4) and (0, 4), so there are 5. The inequality x + 2y ≤ 20 holds at all of them (its largest value is 10 at (2, 4)), so it cuts nothing off; counting every inequality that is written (6 in all) would give 6.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Mathematics Part II, Ch 12 Linear Programming: feasible region, corner points and a redundant constraint

subject: mathematics
stem: The number of reflexive relations that can be defined on a set containing 3 elements is:
explanation: A reflexive relation on a 3-element set must contain the 3 pairs (a, a), while each of the other 3 × 3 − 3 = 6 ordered pairs may be included or left out freely. So there are 2^6 = 64 reflexive relations. The value 512 = 2^9 counts every relation on the set, and 8 = 2^3 wrongly counts choices on the three pairs that are compulsory.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Mathematics Part I, Ch 1 Relations and Functions: reflexive relations on a small finite set

subject: mathematics
stem: The curve x² + xy + y² = 7 passes through the point (1, 2). For this curve, dy/dx at (1, 2) equals:
explanation: Differentiate both sides with respect to x, applying the product rule to xy: 2x + y + x(dy/dx) + 2y(dy/dx) = 0, so dy/dx = −(2x + y)/(x + 2y). At (1, 2) this is −(2 + 2)/(1 + 4) = −4/5. Dropping the y that the product rule produces gives −2/5, and inverting the fraction gives −5/4.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Mathematics Part I, Ch 5 Continuity and Differentiability: derivative of implicit functions

subject: mathematics
stem: A curve is given parametrically by x = t² and y = t³, where t is a real parameter. The second derivative d²y/dx² at t = 2 equals:
explanation: Here dy/dx = (dy/dt)/(dx/dt) = 3t²/2t = 3t/2. Then d²y/dx² = [d/dt(3t/2)]/(dx/dt) = (3/2)/(2t) = 3/(4t), which is 3/8 at t = 2. Stopping at d/dt(3t/2) gives 3/2, and dividing d²y/dt² by dx/dt gives 12/4 = 3.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Mathematics Part I, Ch 5 Continuity and Differentiability: parametric differentiation and second order derivatives

stem:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I (function)
(A) e^(3x)
(B) log_e (3x)
(C) tan⁻¹(3x)
(D) sin⁻¹ x
List-II (derivative with respect to x)
(I) 1/x
(II) 3/(1 + 9x²)
(III) 1/√(1 − x²)
(IV) 3e^(3x)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: By the chain rule, d/dx e^(3x) = 3e^(3x), d/dx log_e (3x) = 3/(3x) = 1/x and d/dx tan⁻¹(3x) = 3/(1 + 9x²), while d/dx sin⁻¹ x = 1/√(1 − x²). The factor 3 from the inner function survives in the exponential and in the tan⁻¹ result but cancels in the logarithm.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Mathematics Part I, Ch 5 Continuity and Differentiability: derivatives of exponential, logarithmic and inverse trigonometric functions

subject: mathematics
stem: The function f(x) = x² − 2 log_e x, with domain x > 0, is strictly increasing on which of the following intervals?
explanation: f′(x) = 2x − 2/x = 2(x² − 1)/x. For x > 0 the sign of f′ is the sign of x² − 1, which is positive only when x > 1, so f increases on (1, ∞). On (0, 1) the derivative is negative, so that is where f decreases; (0, ∞) wrongly treats x² as the only term.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Mathematics Part I, Ch 6 Application of Derivatives: increasing and decreasing functions

subject: mathematics
stem: Two positive numbers x and y satisfy x + y = 12. The maximum value of x²y is:
explanation: Put y = 12 − x, so f(x) = 12x² − x³. Then f′(x) = 24x − 3x² = 3x(8 − x) = 0 gives x = 8, and f″(8) = 24 − 48 < 0, so this is a maximum. With y = 4 the value is 8² × 4 = 256. Splitting the sum equally, x = y = 6, gives only 216.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Mathematics Part I, Ch 6 Application of Derivatives: maxima and minima, second derivative test and optimisation

subject: mathematics
stem: Suppose f is an integrable function on [0, 4] such that ∫ from 0 to 4 of f(x) dx = 7 and ∫ from 2 to 4 of f(x) dx = 3. Then ∫ from 0 to 2 of (2f(x) + 1) dx is equal to:
explanation: By additivity, ∫ from 0 to 2 of f(x) dx = 7 − 3 = 4. Then ∫ from 0 to 2 of (2f(x) + 1) dx = 2(4) + [x] from 0 to 2 = 8 + 2 = 10. Treating the integral of the constant 1 over [0, 2] as 1 instead of 2 gives 9, and adding 7 and 3 instead of subtracting gives 22.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Mathematics Part II, Ch 7 Integrals: properties of definite integrals (additivity and linearity)

subject: mathematics
stem: The integral of x log_e x with respect to x, taken from 1 to e, equals:
explanation: Integrating by parts with u = log_e x and dv = x dx gives (x²/2) log_e x − x²/4. At x = e this is e²/2 − e²/4 = e²/4, and at x = 1 it is −1/4, so the value is e²/4 + 1/4 = (e² + 1)/4. Subtracting 1/4 instead of adding it gives (e² − 1)/4.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Mathematics Part II, Ch 7 Integrals: integration by parts and evaluation of a definite integral

subject: mathematics
stem: Find the area lying under the curve y = x² + 2 between the vertical lines x = 1 and x = 4.
explanation: Area = ∫ from 1 to 4 of (x² + 2) dx = [x³/3 + 2x] from 1 to 4 = (64/3 + 8) − (1/3 + 2) = 21 + 6 = 27. Leaving out the 2x term gives only 21, and forgetting to divide x³ by 3 gives 69.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Mathematics Part II, Ch 8 Application of Integrals: area under a curve between two ordinates

subject: mathematics
stem: The parabola y = 4x − x² cuts the x-axis at two points. The area between the parabola and the x-axis is:
explanation: The parabola meets the x-axis where 4x − x² = 0, that is at x = 0 and x = 4, and lies above the axis between them. Area = ∫ from 0 to 4 of (4x − x²) dx = [2x² − x³/3] from 0 to 4 = 32 − 64/3 = 32/3. Integrating only 4x gives 32, which ignores the −x² term.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Mathematics Part II, Ch 8 Application of Integrals: area between a parabola and the x-axis

subject: mathematics
stem: The area of the region bounded by y = x³, the x-axis and the ordinates x = −1 and x = 2 equals:
explanation: The curve lies below the x-axis for −1 < x < 0 and above it for 0 < x < 2, so the two parts are added as positive areas: ∫ from −1 to 0 of |x³| dx = 1/4 and ∫ from 0 to 2 of x³ dx = 4, giving 17/4. The single integral from −1 to 2 gives 15/4, which lets the negative part cancel instead of adding.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Mathematics Part II, Ch 8 Application of Integrals: area under a curve when the curve crosses the axis

subject: mathematics
stem: If y = y(x) satisfies dy/dx = (x + y)/x for x > 0 with y(1) = 2, then y(e) equals:
explanation: Put y = vx, so v + x(dv/dx) = 1 + v and dv = dx/x, giving v = log_e x + C and y = x log_e x + Cx. The condition y(1) = 2 gives C = 2, so y(e) = e(1 + 2) = 3e. Writing y = x log_e x + 2 loses the factor x on the constant and gives e + 2.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Mathematics Part II, Ch 9 Differential Equations: homogeneous equations of first order and first degree

subject: mathematics
stem:
Consider the following statements:
(A) Eliminating the constant A from y = Ax² gives the differential equation x(dy/dx) = 2y.
(B) The equation dy/dx = (x² + y²)/(xy) is homogeneous.
(C) The equation dy/dx = y/x has the solution y = x + C, where C is a constant.
(D) Separating the variables in dy/dx = x/y leads to y² − x² = C.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: From y = Ax², dy/dx = 2Ax = 2y/x, so x(dy/dx) = 2y and (A) is true. Scaling x and y by the same factor leaves (x² + y²)/(xy) unchanged, so (B) is true. Separating dy/y = dx/x gives y = Cx, not y = x + C, so (C) is false. Separating y dy = x dx gives y² = x² + 2K, which is y² − x² = C, so (D) is true.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Mathematics Part II, Ch 9 Differential Equations: forming an equation from a family of curves, homogeneous equations and variable separable solutions

subject: mathematics
stem: For the first order differential equation y dx − (x + 2y²) dy = 0, the integrating factor is:
explanation: Dividing by dy gives dx/dy − x/y = 2y, which is linear in x with P = −1/y. The integrating factor is e^(∫P dy) = e^(−log_e y) = 1/y. Taking P as +1/y instead gives the factor y, a sign slip.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Mathematics Part II, Ch 9 Differential Equations: linear equation dx/dy + Px = Q and its integrating factor

subject: mathematics
stem: The diagonals of a parallelogram are represented by the vectors i + 2j + 2k and 3i − 2j + 2k. The area of the parallelogram, in square units, is:
explanation: The cross product of the diagonals is (8, 4, −8), with magnitude √(64 + 16 + 64) = 12. The parallelogram has half this area, 12/2 = 6. Using 12 forgets the half, and 3√17/2 is half the product of the diagonal lengths, valid only when the diagonals are perpendicular.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Mathematics Part II, Ch 10 Vector Algebra: vector (cross) product and area of a parallelogram with given diagonals

subject: mathematics
stem:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
(A) Non-zero vectors a and b are perpendicular
(B) Non-zero vectors a and b are parallel
(C) Area of the parallelogram with adjacent sides a and b
(D) Unit vector in the direction of a
List-II
(I) |a × b|
(II) a · b = 0
(III) a/|a|
(IV) a × b = 0
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: Perpendicular vectors have a zero dot product, a · b = 0, while parallel vectors have a zero cross product, a × b = 0. The magnitude |a × b| is the area of the parallelogram on a and b, and a/|a| is the unit vector along a. Swapping the dot and cross conditions is the usual mistake.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Mathematics Part II, Ch 10 Vector Algebra: dot product, cross product and unit vector

subject: mathematics
stem: The lines (x − 1)/4 = (y + 2)/k = (z − 3)/2 and (x + 3)/3 = (y − 1)/(−2) = (z + 5)/(−1) are perpendicular to each other. The value of k is:
explanation: The direction ratios are (4, k, 2) and (3, −2, −1). Perpendicular lines have a zero dot product, so 4(3) + k(−2) + 2(−1) = 12 − 2k − 2 = 0, giving k = 5. A sign slip on the last term gives 7, and ignoring the third components gives 6.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Mathematics Part II, Ch 11 Three Dimensional Geometry: direction ratios and perpendicular lines

subject: mathematics
stem: A straight line passes through the points (−2, 1, 5) and (0, 4, 9). The z-coordinate of the point on this line whose x-coordinate is 4 is:
explanation: The direction ratios are (0 + 2, 4 − 1, 9 − 5) = (2, 3, 4), so a general point is (−2 + 2t, 1 + 3t, 5 + 4t). Putting x = 4 gives −2 + 2t = 4, so t = 3 and z = 5 + 12 = 17. Treating the starting x as +2 gives t = 1 and z = 9, while taking t = x/2 = 2 gives 13.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Mathematics Part II, Ch 11 Three Dimensional Geometry: Cartesian equation of a line through two points

subject: mathematics
stem: Taking principal values, the value of cos⁻¹(−1/2) + sin⁻¹(−√3/2) + tan⁻¹(−1) is:
explanation: The principal values are cos⁻¹(−1/2) = 2π/3, sin⁻¹(−√3/2) = −π/3 and tan⁻¹(−1) = −π/4. The sum is 2π/3 − π/3 − π/4 = π/3 − π/4 = π/12. Taking tan⁻¹(−1) as 3π/4, which lies outside the principal range, gives 13π/12.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Mathematics Part I, Ch 2 Inverse Trigonometric Functions: principal value branches and values at negative arguments

subject: mathematics
stem: Three machines A, B and C produce 50%, 30% and 20% of the items in a factory. Of their items, 2%, 5% and 10% respectively are defective. An item chosen at random is found to be defective. The probability that machine B made it is:
explanation: By total probability, P(defective) = 0.5 × 0.02 + 0.3 × 0.05 + 0.2 × 0.10 = 0.010 + 0.015 + 0.020 = 0.045. By Bayes theorem, P(B | defective) = 0.015/0.045 = 1/3. The value 3/10 is only the share of output from B, ignoring the evidence, and 4/9 is the corresponding value for C.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Mathematics Part II, Ch 13 Probability: total probability theorem and Bayes theorem

stem: A galvanometer of resistance 99 Ω gives full-scale deflection for a current of 10 mA. It is converted into an ammeter of range 0 to 1 A by connecting a shunt. The resistance of the ammeter so formed is:
explanation: For the shunt, Ig × G = (I − Ig) × S, so S = (0.010 × 99)/(1 − 0.010) = 1.0 Ω. The shunt is in parallel with the galvanometer, so the ammeter resistance is G S/(G + S) = 99 × 1.0/100 = 0.99 Ω, which also equals Ig G/I = 0.99/1. Quoting 1.0 Ω gives only the shunt, 100 Ω adds the two resistances as if in series, and 99 Ω ignores the shunt altogether.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Physics Part I, Ch 4 Moving Charges and Magnetism: moving coil galvanometer, conversion to an ammeter with a shunt and the resulting resistance

subject: physics
unit: Magnetic Effects of Current and Magnetism
stem: A beam of singly charged ions enters a region where a uniform electric field of 3.0 × 10^4 V/m and a uniform magnetic field of 0.10 T act at right angles to each other and to the beam. Ions of which speed pass through undeflected?
explanation: Ions pass undeflected when the electric and magnetic forces balance, qE = qvB, so v = E/B = 3.0 × 10^4 / 0.10 = 3.0 × 10^5 m/s. The charge and the mass cancel, so every singly charged ion with this speed goes straight. The product E × B = 3.0 × 10^3 has the wrong dimensions for a speed.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Physics Part I, Ch 4 Moving Charges and Magnetism: motion of a charge in combined electric and magnetic fields (velocity selector)

subject: physics
